title: Spec test adequacy
description: Reusable proof-quality columns applied to every current test-requiring spec clause. The clause is the row; these criteria are the columns. Evaluations pin an exact spec revision and evidence bundle rather than grading a plan-wide pile of tests.

criteria.title: Proof traces to the exact current spec revision
criteria.model: Every graded row names the canonical plan/spec/revision and is backed by one or more immutable work-item evidence bindings for that exact revision.
criteria.method: Resolve the clause through plans:get-specs and its bindings through plans:get-spec-evidence; compare exact spec id, revision, and fingerprint rather than filenames or prose claims.
criteria.driftMarkers: A green test file with no spec edge; a VAL alias that was not resolved; evidence for an older revision treated as current.

criteria.title: Fixtures represent the intended boundary
criteria.model: Where a fixture is required or used, its calibration to the clause's real boundary is demonstrated and fingerprinted; fixture-free proof is explicitly not applicable.
criteria.method: Inspect fixture bindings/fingerprints and their adequacy.fixtureCalibrated attestation; reject synthetic or stale fixtures that cannot reproduce the relevant state.
criteria.driftMarkers: A fixture that cannot trigger the behavior; production-only state replaced by an uncalibrated mock; changed fixture bytes under an old fingerprint.

criteria.title: The proof can fail when the behavior is wrong
criteria.model: At least one bound check has a demonstrated counterexample, mutant, pre-fix failure, or equally concrete falsification path.
criteria.method: Read the bound mutation/counterexample evidence or adequacy.falsifiable attestation and confirm the negative control changes the verdict.
criteria.driftMarkers: Assertions that only prove code executed; snapshots that bless any output; a test never observed red.

criteria.title: Required layers reach the real path
criteria.model: Every layer named by the clause is represented by bound proof and the exercised path reaches the implementation boundary the clause describes.
criteria.method: Compare requiredTestLayers with adequacy.testLayer on bindings and require adequacy.pathReachable for each required layer.
criteria.driftMarkers: A unit double offered for an integration contract; the intended handler or transport never reached; one required layer silently absent.

criteria.title: The oracle is independent of the implementation
criteria.model: The expected result comes from the behavioral contract, an external invariant, or an independent computation—not the same implementation under test.
criteria.method: Inspect adequacy.oracleIndependent and the evidence reference; identify the source of expected truth and verify it is not copied from the implementation path.
criteria.driftMarkers: Expected values generated by the function under test; mock and implementation sharing the same bug; circular snapshot approval.

criteria.title: The proof was collected, executed, and passed
criteria.model: Applicable tests/checks were collected, were not skipped, executed against the claimed environment, and produced a successful current outcome.
criteria.method: Require non-skipped collection and execution metadata plus a passing/killed outcome; a testRun reference without a verdict is unknown, never pass.
criteria.driftMarkers: Zero collected tests; skipped/quarantined proof; compile-only evidence; a stale ledger row mistaken for a fresh run.

criteria.title: Every relied-on fingerprint is current
criteria.model: Spec, source, test, fixture, rubric, environment, coverage, and run references are current for the evaluation; missing current fingerprints remain unknown.
criteria.method: Use plans:get-spec-evidence currentness. Any stale dimension fails; any unresolved applicable dimension is unknown.
criteria.driftMarkers: Old green evidence after a spec/source/test change; absent current fingerprints reported as current; pruned coverage/run rows ignored.

criteria.title: Proof meets the plan-class and behavior-risk floor
criteria.model: The reusable plan-class policy supplies the floor. Feature work normally requires targeted L3 intent proof; bugfixes, migrations, mutation-required clauses, and high-risk authorization/concurrency/lifecycle/data-integrity behavior require targeted L4 hardening unless an explicit current waiver exists.
criteria.method: Resolve the plan class and behavior class, then inspect coverage rung flags or successful targeted mutation/counterexample proof. For L4 waivers require justification, approvalRef, and a non-expired expiresAt when present.
criteria.driftMarkers: Depth >= N used instead of the independent meets_lN flag; a broad mutation run with no link to this clause; an unapproved or expired waiver.

criteria.title: No author-disclosed hole travels with a passing proof
criteria.model: A disclosure recorded on a binding is an admission that the bound evidence does not fully establish the clause, so it can never coexist with a machine PASS. Any non-empty disclosed gap fails and the disclosed text is named in the blocking reason; a clause whose active bindings record no disclosure is not applicable.
criteria.method: Read adequacy.disclosedGap on every active binding for the clause. Fail when any is non-empty, naming the disclosed text in the would-block reason rather than leaving it unread on the row; report not-applicable only when no active binding carries a disclosure.
criteria.driftMarkers: A known hole recorded on the binding while the verdict still reads pass; a disclosure demoted to prose in an evidence blob that no evaluator field reads; a gap treated as mitigated by re-binding without closing it.
